_README: One point-to-point ARQ link, described ONCE, for both machines to share.
MANUALLY maintained for now: copy this file to
/workspace/experiments/settings/link.json
fill in your two radios, and run  ./auto_link.sh  on EACH machine.
auto_link.sh reads this, works out which end THIS box is (by matching a
radio serial it can see), and runs the whole pipeline for that end:
read role  ->  prepare.sh (survey THIS box's receive band)
->  calibration.sh (measure sync-threshold on the TX->RX link,
both ends agreeing through the shared file)
->  one resolved parameter file  ->  radio.sh
ROLES. 'source' TRANSMITS the data and RECEIVES the ACK. 'sink' RECEIVES the
data and TRANSMITS the ACK. Each box's RECEIVE path is the one surveyed:
the sink surveys the DATA band, the source surveys the ACK band.
FREQUENCIES. data.freq_hz is where the source transmits and the sink listens;
ack.freq_hz is where the sink transmits and the source listens. Each is set one
of two ways, and you choose per direction:
a NUMBER -> pinned. Both ends use exactly this carrier.
null     -> survey-driven. The box that RECEIVES that direction picks the
quiet spot its prepare.sh survey found (the sink picks the data
carrier, the source picks the ACK carrier), publishes it to
link-state.json beside this file, and the far end reads it there.
Neither end ever types it, so the two cannot tune apart.
Survey-driven is usually better: only the receiver's own survey knows what is
actually quiet in ITS room. Pin one when you must (a licence, a filter, another
experiment) and leave the other null. prepare.sh also saves every carrier it
found to searching/freqs-<timestamp>.json.
ACK TRANSPORT. 'rf' carries the ACK over a second RF path (full-duplex: one
radio, two RF ports, data and ACK on different frequencies) — fill in ack.*
and each role's ack:{subdev,ant,gain}. 'tcp' carries the ACK over the network
instead — set ack.host (the sink's site/host) and ack.port, drop the RF ack
fields. det-mult and sync-threshold are NOT set here: they are MEASURED and
read back from the survey/calibration profile.
